content.topic: Anticoagulation in pregnancy (selected guidance from page)

monitoring.summary: Serial measurements of plasma anti-activated coagulation factor X activity to guide LMWH dosing remain of uncertain clinical benefit; assay limitations and lack of optimal target levels are noted. Monitoring may be reserved for high-risk circumstances (recurrent VTE, renal impairment, extremes of body weight).

anticoagulants_and_safety.LMWH: Preferred in pregnancy; predictable pharmacokinetics. Data lacking on frequent weight-based dose adjustments and on bone loss risk.
anticoagulants_and_safety.UFH: Associated with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and bone loss; used in some high-risk situations and prior to delivery conversion.
anticoagulants_and_safety.Fondaparinux: May be considered for allergy/adverse response to LMWH though data limited; minor transplacental passage demonstrated.
anticoagulants_and_safety.VKAs_and_Warfarin: VKAs cross placenta and are associated with embryopathy in first trimester; third-trimester use can cause fetal/neonatal hemorrhage and placental abruption. Warfarin may be associated with fetal CNS anomalies.

labour_delivery_management.summary: Planned delivery is recommended for women on therapeutic LMWH in collaboration with a multidisciplinary team to avoid spontaneous labor while anticoagulated. If regional analgesia is considered, an interval (example: ~24 h) should elapse since last therapeutic LMWH dose (assuming normal renal function). In high-risk situations (eg recent PE) conversion to UFH ~36 h prior to delivery is recommended; UFH infusion should be stopped a specified period (eg several hours) prior to anticipated delivery and normal APTT confirmed before regional anesthesia.
labour_delivery_management.postpartum_reinitiation: Timing of post-partum reinitiation of LMWH is limited and should depend on mode of delivery and thrombosis vs bleeding risk. LMWH generally withheld for ~4 h after epidural catheter removal; interim prophylactic dosing may be considered post-operatively once safe intervals have elapsed.

content.evidence_notes: Cohort study cited: bone mineral density measured 4–7 years after last delivery in 152 women (92 received prolonged LMWH) showed similar lumbar spine BMD after adjustment; no osteoporosis/osteoporotic fractures reported.

Associated Conditions: Monitoring of anticoagulation during LMWH therapy in pregnancy
genes.context: References to 'plasma anti-activated coagulation factor X activity' and 'anti-activated coagulation factor X monitoring' as a potential way to guide LMWH dosing in pregnancy, reserved for high-risk circumstances such as recurrent VTE, renal impairment, and extremes of body weight.
